name: Plus 15 Skywalk Network
description: Traverse above the bustling downtown streets through the world's most extensive skywalk network—a winter-proof maze connecting shimmering glass towers, hidden atriums, and vibrant plazas.
personalNote: The bridges are 15 feet above ground, hence the name +15. Individual bridges and building hours varies, but most are open until 6 PM.

name: Calgary Tower
description: Stand atop a glass floor 191 meters above the heart of the city and enjoy a 360-degree panorama of downtown skyscrapers all the way to the majestic Rocky Mountains.
personalNote: There is a rotating restaurant in the tower that is actually quite good and not a tourist trap.

name: Stephen Avenue Walk
description: Stroll down Calgary’s historic pedestrian street, where 19th-century sandstone architecture intersect towering skyscrapers.
personalNote: Pairs naturally with the Calgary Tower and CORE shopping centre.

name: The Bow and Wonderland
description: Behold Foster + Partners' curving architectural masterpiece, then stand awestruck beneath Jaume Plensa’s monumental 'Wonderland' wire-mesh head framing the city skyline.
personalNote: A quick stop that works well as part of a downtown walking route.

name: Calgary Central Library
description: Step inside an architectural masterpiece—a dazzling, light-filled cathedral of books and community where cascading wood stairs and soaring curves redefine modern design.
personalNote: Sign up for a free tour of the library while you're inside!

name: Studio Bell, home of the National Music Centre
description: Plug into Canada’s sonic heartbeat inside a shimmering terracotta-clad architectural marvel packed with legendary instruments, interactive sound booths, and rock-and-roll history.
personalNote: Combine it with the Central Library and an onward walk toward Inglewood.

name: Inglewood Main Street
description: Wander Calgary’s oldest neighbourhood, where indie shops, vintage vaults, cutting-edge art galleries, and craft breweries shine against a backdrop of historic relics.
personalNote: Best treated as a flexible wandering stop rather than one fixed attraction.

name: Peace Bridge
description: Stroll across Santiago Calatrava’s futuristic red-and-white helix bridge—a striking kinetic sculpture spanning gracefully over the Bow River.
personalNote: Particularly photogenic in the evening and easy to pair with the RiverWalk.
address: Peace Bridge, Bow River Path (North), Calgary, AB
bestTime: Evening in summer; daylight in winter

name: Prince’s Island Park
description: Escape to a tranquil island tucked in the middle of the Bow River, where willow-shaded trails, fluttering ducks, and vibrant festival grounds await.
personalNote: A good reset between downtown sightseeing stops.
bestTime: Summer evening or any clear day

name: Heritage Park Historical Village
description: Time-travel to Western Canada’s pioneer era across a sprawling living-history village complete with steam trains, vintage midway rides, and costumed townsfolk.
personalNote: Plan for at least half a day and check the operating calendar to plan the day.

name: Bowness Park
description: Unwind beside a glistening river lagoon in a beloved park where summer paddleboats and winter ice-skating trails create pure seasonal magic.
personalNote: Summer boating and winter skating give the park very different personalities.

name: Fish Creek Provincial Park - West
description: Lose yourself in one of North America’s largest urban provincial parks, where wild deer graze through ancient cottonwood forests and sun-dappled creek trails.
personalNote: Choose a specific entrance or trailhead before visiting; the park is very large.
address: Fish Creek Provincial Park, Calgary, AB

name: Fish Creek Provincial Park — East Entrance
description: Discover the secluded eastern gateway to Fish Creek, where historic Bow Valley Ranch buildings meet tranquil riverside pathways and whispering aspen groves.
personalNote: Use this east-side entrance when exploring the park from Bow Bottom Trail; conditions and access can vary by season.
address: Bow Valley Ranch, 15975 Bow Bottom Trail SE, Calgary, AB

name: The Family of Man
description: Gaze up at Mario Armengol’s iconic bronze figures standing tall against the skyline, representing the enduring spirit of humanity in the heart of downtown.
personalNote: A quick public-art stop near The Bow and Stephen Avenue.

name: 10th & 10th Mural
description: Turn the corner into an open-air gallery where vibrant, larger-than-life street art transforms an ordinary downtown intersection into a striking visual landmark.
personalNote: Pin the mural itself rather than treating the whole block as the destination.
address: First on Tenth, 123 10 Avenue SW, Calgary, AB

name: CORE Shopping Centre and Devonian Gardens
description: Shop under soaring glass vaults before stepping directly into a lush, tropical indoor jungle hidden high above the downtown streets.
personalNote: A useful indoor stop in winter and a natural Plus 15 connection.

name: Eighth Avenue Place
description: Soak in the soaring, light-soaked architecture and striking art installations of one of downtown’s most elegant corporate and cultural crossroads.
personalNote: Use it as a Plus 15 connection from CORE; has a Starbucks.

name: Udderly Art Pasture
description: Spot an unexpected herd of whimsically painted, larger-than-life fiberglass cows adding a splash of quirky artistic joy to the urban streetscape.
personalNote: The current legacy display is associated with Centennial Parkade; confirm the display before visiting.

name: 17th Avenue SW
description: Dive headfirst into Calgary’s legendary 'Red Mile,' where sun-soaked patios, trendy boutiques, and world-class culinary hotspots pulse with electric energy.
personalNote: Best explored as a flexible evening stroll rather than a single stop.
address: 17 Avenue SW and 8 Street SW, Calgary, AB
bestTime: Evening for nightlife; daytime for shopping

name: BUMP Mural Project — World’s Tallest Mural
description: Tilt your head all the way back to marvel at a jaw-dropping monumental skyscraper mural that turns Calgary's skyline into a living canvas.
personalNote: Pinned to First on Tenth at 123 10 Avenue SW, the location of the world’s-tallest-mural project.
address: First on Tenth, 123 10 Avenue SW, Calgary, AB

name: Lougheed House
description: Step back into the opulent Victorian era inside a magnificent 1891 sandstone estate surrounded by immaculately manicured historic gardens.
personalNote: A calmer contrast to the restaurants and nightlife of 17th Avenue.

name: The Confluence Historic Site and Parkland
description: Stand at the sacred meeting of the Bow and Elbow Rivers, where centuries of Indigenous heritage and Calgary’s founding stories come alive in expansive parklands.
personalNote: The site is the modern successor to the Fort Calgary location and redevelopment.

name: St. Patrick’s Island
description: Cross over to an award-winning island escape featuring sculptural play spaces, pebble beaches, a dramatic rising lookout mound, and tranquil river channels.
personalNote: A natural extension of an East Village and RiverWalk outing.

name: Esker Foundation
description: Immerse your senses in thought-provoking, cutting-edge contemporary art inside a sunlit, beautifully curated gallery space overlooking Inglewood.
personalNote: Check the current exhibition and hours before building it into a route.

name: Crescent Heights Lookout / McHugh Bluff
description: Conquer the scenic wooden staircase to the clifftop rim for an unbeatable, postcard-worthy panorama of the downtown skyline framed by the river valley.
personalNote: One of the strongest skyline viewpoints in the city; allow time for the stairs.
bestTime: Evening in summer; daylight in winter

name: Eau Claire Plaza
description: Bask in riverside relaxation at a vibrant downtown gathering square where shimmering fountains and bustling pathway cyclists set the rhythm of the city.
personalNote: Check current construction and access conditions before visiting.

name: RiverWalk — West Side
description: Cruise along golden riverbanks on sun-drenched pathways linking Calgary’s finest parks, bridges, and waterside vistas.
personalNote: Connect it with Eau Claire, Prince’s Island Park, and Peace Bridge.

name: Gasoline Alley Museum
description: Marvel at a breathtaking collection of pristine vintage automobiles, neon signs, and early 20th-century Americana frozen in golden-age splendour.
personalNote: It is included with Heritage Park admission and is worth allowing extra time for.

name: Baker Park
description: Unwind in immaculate formal riverside gardens featuring sweeping lawns, reflecting pools, and serene picnic spots overlooking the bend of the Bow.
personalNote: A natural pairing with Bowness Park, although they are not the same park.

name: Nose Hill Park
description: Roam free across one of North America’s largest municipal parks, where native grassland prairies, grazing wildlife, and boundless mountain horizons stretch forever.
personalNote: Choose a trailhead before visiting because the park has many entrances.

name: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary
description: Slip into a tranquil, wildlife-rich sanctuary where whispering wetlands and shaded forest trails offer a serene escape from the urban rush.
personalNote: A quieter alternative to the busier Inglewood commercial strip.

name: North Glenmore Park
description: Bask in sparkling reservoir vistas and gentle breezes along scenic waterfront trails in this beloved lakeside haven.
personalNote: Good for a slower walk, especially when paired with Glenmore Reservoir activities.

name: Bow River Rafting from Edworthy Park
description: Ride the glacial currents on a relaxing summer river float, paddling crystal-clear waters beneath wide-open Albertan skies.
personalNote: There are a few raft rental companies who also offer shuttle buses back to the starting point. Check their websites for details.

name: Calgary Zoo
description: Embark on a wild global safari across lush botanical gardens and immersive animal habitats at one of Canada’s premier zoos.
personalNote: Arrive early for a more comfortable visit and better animal activity.

name: WinSport / Canada Olympic Park
description: Feed your adrenaline at Calgary’s legendary Olympic playground, featuring downhill karting, soaring ziplines, and world-class athletic thrills.
personalNote: Downhill karting and other activities are seasonal; check the current calendar.
address: 88 Canada Olympic Road SW, Calgary, AB

name: Cobb’s Adventure Park
description: Dive into pure family-friendly pandemonium across bouncy pillows, petting farms, mini-golf courses, and action-packed outdoor mazes.
personalNote: Confirm the current opening dates and activities before visiting.

name: SAM Centre and Calgary Stampede Grounds
description: Saddle up for an immersive, high-tech celebration of Calgary’s legendary cowboy culture and Stampede history.
personalNote: Check whether the Stampede itself is operating before planning a grounds visit.
address: 1911 Big Four Trail SE, Calgary, AB
bestTime: Daytime; check hours and event dates

name: The Hangar Flight Museum
description: Walk among legendary vintage aircraft and aerospace marvels that chronicle Canada’s daring aviation pioneers.
personalNote: A good indoor option and an easy pairing with the Calgary Zoo area.

name: TELUS Spark Science Centre
description: Ignite your imagination across mind-bending interactive galleries, high-tech maker labs, and dazzling planetarium dome shows.
personalNote: Allow several hours if visiting with children; check special programming in advance.
address: 220 St. George’s Drive NE, Calgary, AB
